summary: Candidate A directly implements the frozen contract with minimal, repository-pattern-aligned changes. Candidate B adds explicitly out-of-scope retry machinery and duplicates FilesService.Add instead of routing through it.
reasons: A adds the exact Upload signature, validates filename/content, uses multipartbody.NewFile("file", ...), and delegates to Add with unchanged options.
A’s tests cover multipart field/name/content, retry of non-seekable streamed content, pre-request validation, and source-reader error propagation.
B violates the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add by duplicating its option handling, request construction, decoding, and error behavior.

B changes RawClient behavior for all seekable request bodies, including Content-Length and ownership/Close semantics, despite the contract forbidding unrelated retry refactoring and requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged.
risks_b: wireSeekableRequestBody can leave a reader positioned at EOF if seeking back to the original offset fails after a successful seek to the end.
Its GetBody closure reuses and mutates one shared ReadSeeker, which is more fragile than producing independent replay bodies.
B lacks the contract-requested Upload source-reader failure test and introduces broad changelog/API claims beyond the requested scope.
